clue.text: Neat design suggested by a nautical engineer

definitions.meaning: tidy and in good order, as a well-run vessel should be

definitions.text: design suggested by a nautical engineer
definitions.meaning: read literally, the outline or form a naval architect would draw for a vessel

explanation.surface: A tidy plan put forward by a marine engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means trim and orderly, from the tidiness demanded aboard a vessel; read literally it is the form of a seagoing hull.

clue.text: Lean over a foot back

definitions.meaning: of a boat, to tilt or list to one side
the rear part of the human foot

explanation.surface: Someone tilts forward over a foot that points backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that lists is said to do this; the same word names the rounded rear of the foot below the ankle.

clue.text: American tract for a couple with a song that is

parts.note: PR is the standard abbreviation for pair, a couple
an air is a tune or song
IE is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A stretch of America is set aside for a pair who come with a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The grassland plains of the American Midwest are a vast tract of treeless land.

clue.text: Would it aid drinking from a lady's slipper the very last drop of wine?

definitions.text: Would it aid drinking from a lady's slipper
definitions.meaning: a playful reading: a tap fitted at the heel of a shoe would let the champagne out of a slipper

definitions.text: the very last drop of wine
definitions.meaning: the dregs left at the bottom of a glass after drinking

explanation.surface: A romantic toast of wine from a lady's shoe, drained to the dregs.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is an old word for the liquor left in a glass after drinking; the joke imagines a spout in a shoe's heel.

clue.text: Maybe North South or Eastern European

definitions.meaning: either end of the Earth's axis, north or south, as an example
a native of Poland in Eastern Europe

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a direction or a region of Europe is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The ends of the Earth's axis are the North and South ones; a person from Poland is called by the same word.

clue.text: Articles of clothing are her daily concern

definitions.text: Articles of clothing are her daily concern

parts.words: Articles of clothing are her daily concern
parts.note: the articles are the pieces she commissions on clothes for a newspaper or magazine, so a journalist in charge of a style section is meant

explanation.surface: A woman whose everyday preoccupation is what to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who runs the style pages commissions written articles about clothes every day.

clue.text: Employ ESP material to secure a sitting

parts.note: to take on staff is to employ them
taken as written
lace is a delicate fabric

explanation.surface: Hiring someone with psychic powers to get a seat at a séance.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit down in the seat allotted to you is to claim a seat, or occupy a sitting position.

clue.text: A mendacious young shaver?

parts.note: a young shaver is a boy, but read literally a youth whose face has no beard yet, and mendacious means lying

explanation.surface: A lying little boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A shameless teller of untruths is one with an unblushing, unbearded face, which suits a lad too young to shave.

clue.text: Prepare kindling for getting a meal of chop suey

definitions.meaning: cut up wood into small sticks for lighting a fire

definitions.text: for getting a meal of chop suey
definitions.meaning: one of the pair of slim utensils used to eat Chinese food

explanation.surface: Getting the fire going before eating Chinese food.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is cutting firewood; as one it is an eating utensil used in pairs in East Asia.

clue.text: Severely criticise short hemlines!

definitions.meaning: to scold or reprimand sharply
a playful reading: a frock whose hem has been lowered or is low on the body

explanation.surface: Someone harshly condemns miniskirts.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a severe telling-off is an idiom; read literally, a frock low down, the opposite of a short hemline.

clue.text: Semi-detached houses raising a peal of derision

indicators.note: a semi-detached property is a pair of homes joined side by side, so the abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Neighbours in a pair of joined homes laugh scornfully.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-detached house in Britain is one of a pair sharing a wall, which is why the clue gives two copies of HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A mocking laugh is written as a repeated syllable, a burst of scornful laughter.

clue.text: Right pronunciation is of no significance if you communicate this way

indicators.note: the clue points to how the word Right is spoken, which matches another spelling

parts.note: the word as spoken, which sounds the same as the method of communication

explanation.surface: Pronunciation does not matter when you put things on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: when you put words on paper nobody hears them, so a word said like Right but spelt differently loses nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting words on paper is a way of conveying a message without speaking.

clue.text: Don river

definitions.meaning: to put on clothing
a river in north-east England flowing through Durham and Sunderland

explanation.surface: The River Don is named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don river' looks like the River Don in Yorkshire, but Don is a verb, to put on clothes. The other sense is the river of Durham in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To have clothes on is the other verb; the river runs through Durham to the North Sea.

clue.text: Leaves with all debts settled

definitions.meaning: goes away from, abandons
even, with nothing owed either way

explanation.surface: Someone departs once every debt is paid off.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gives up a job departs it; and two parties owing nothing to each other are even.

clue.text: Mother must be the one who checks

definitions.meaning: Latin for mother, used in British public-school slang
a playful reading: one who mates, delivering checkmate at chess

explanation.surface: Mum insists on being the one keeping an eye on things.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for a mum was old schoolboy slang; read as a noun from mate, it is a chess player who delivers checkmate.

clue.text: Obtain professional treatment

parts.note: PRO is short for professional
a cure is a course of medical treatment

explanation.surface: Getting expert medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: To get hold of something by effort is to acquire it.

clue.text: Lamentations interpreted by Latin version contained in footnote

indicators.note: the anagram is held inside the footnote's letters

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is a note added at the foot of a letter

indicators.note: a different version of a word is a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Laments translated from Latin appear in a footnote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' signals the anagram of LATIN, giving LAINT, which goes 'contained in' PS.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints and laments are expressions of grief or grievance.

clue.text: Shouted when subjected to therapeutic ministrations

definitions.meaning: in informal British and Australian use, to shout someone is to buy them a drink
given medical care

explanation.surface: Someone yelled while undergoing medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shouted' looks like yelled, but in pub slang to shout is to stand someone a round.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying for someone's drink is standing them one; a patient given medical care has received attention from a doctor.

clue.text: Mischievousness gave old copper a livery disposition

parts.note: D stands for the old British penny, a copper coin before decimalisation in 1971

indicators.note: the letters of the word are disposed, or arranged, afresh

explanation.surface: An old policeman is given a bilious temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old copper' looks like a retired policeman but is the pre-1971 penny, D; 'disposition' turns LIVERY into EVILRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish behaviour is playful naughtiness or wickedness.

clue.text: Well satisfied when record return took the pressure off

indicators.note: a return comes back the other way, so the record's letters are read backwards

parts.note: LP, long-playing, is a vinyl record
to ease is to relieve stress or pressure

explanation.surface: Someone is happy when a record comes back and relieves the strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being content and gratified is a state of happiness with something.

clue.text: One who reads Professional Employment Register to get an employer

parts.note: PER, the initials of the former British government recruitment service
a user is one who employs or makes use of something

explanation.surface: A job-seeker consults a recruitment register to find a boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The Professional Employment Register was a British state jobs service, known by its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies a text carefully is a reader of it.

clue.text: Article from China makes a prominent feature

indicators.note: the article is taken away from the place name

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item from China becomes a striking piece of design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article from China' looks like porcelain, but the article is A, removed from CHINA.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaw's forward point is a facial feature that can jut out.

clue.text: Apparent position of middle letter in 9 down

definitions.meaning: open and plainly visible

definitions.text: position of middle letter in 9 down
definitions.meaning: in the downward entry at 9, the central S sits directly above the letter T

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where the central letter of another answer is placed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9-down answer is CHOPSTICK; its fifth letter S stands directly above T in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in the open is plain to see, not hidden.

clue.text: Not unnaturally it may wind one

definitions.text: Not unnaturally it may wind one

parts.words: Not unnaturally it may wind one
parts.note: a punch to the stomach knocks the breath out of you, and wind does this naturally

explanation.surface: A remark that a punch, quite understandably, leaves you gasping.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch can knock the breath out of a person, and the wind naturally does this too.

clue.text: Finished up apparently

parts.note: finished and up both mean ended, as in time being up

explanation.surface: Something seems to have ended.
explanation.definitionFit: A match or game that has ended is complete, done.

clue.text: The woman's a goddess

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: Declaring that a particular woman is divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen of the Olympian gods in Greek myth, wife of Zeus.

clue.text: Period of patient recovery

parts.note: patient seems to mean calm, but it is someone under medical care getting better

explanation.surface: A time of slow, uncomplaining recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: The time spent recuperating after illness is a stage of regaining health.

clue.text: A Franciscan eminence grise?

definitions.meaning: a member of the order of St Francis, named after the colour of his habit
French for a grey eminence, a power behind the throne, first used of Father Joseph, a Capuchin friar

explanation.surface: A friar of St Francis who is the hidden power behind a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Order of St Francis wore grey habits; read literally, the French phrase names a grey-robed churchman.
